subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency & throughput decision
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Alvarez <sofia@finpay.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency & throughput next steps

Hi Sofia / Alex —

Thanks again for the call today — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap of requirements (what I heard)
- Latency target: p95/p99 important for UI flows — you mentioned p99 should be below ~120–150ms for quick interactions (mostly <=128-token requests).
- Throughput: steady-state ~2k tokens/sec with spikes to ~4–5k tokens/sec during end-of-day batching; peak concurrent requests ~= 200–300.
- Data: no on-prem requirement right now, but sensitive data flows through payment pipelines — want isolation and auditing.

Redwood recommendation (short):
- Pilot: start on Hosted API to validate integration and correctness quickly (fast onboarding + no infra commit).
- Production: for predictable p99 latency and isolation, Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) is the likely fit; Dedicated gives control over autoscale, warm workers, and fixed latency tail.
- Private VPC: only if you need customer-managed networking or on-prem hardware (sounds not required at this stage).

Concrete next steps
1) Can you confirm the p99 target you need for the UI flows (120ms vs 150ms will change the sizing/recommendation)?
2) If you confirm, we can schedule a short performance trial: either a 2-hour spike test on Hosted (to exercise path) or a 1-week Dedicated trial with reserved capacity for production-like runs.
3) I attached a short SLA/latency comparison and a table that maps request sizes to expected p95/p99 numbers for our common model configs.

Proposed meeting to review the trial plan: Thu, Nov 19 at 10am PT — will that work?

If you prefer, Marissa can join to go into pricing/commit options.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Sofia Alvarez <sofia@finpay.com>

Thanks Neha — helpful recap. Confirming the latency/assertions and adding a few specifics from our side: 

What we need to guarantee
- Target p99 for customer-facing UI calls: <= 120ms for requests with payloads up to 128 tokens.
- Background batch traffic is less sensitive to p99 but can create bursts (we see aggregate spikes that approximate 250–300 concurrent inference requests).
- Average request size ~64 tokens, some longer (300–500 tokens) for internal analytics.

Questions
1) How much does Dedicated move the p99 distribution vs Hosted if we keep the same model (e.g., Llama-2-Chat or similar)? Any numbers we can expect for warm vs cold workers?
2) If we go Dedicated, what minimal reserved capacity do you recommend for the 120ms p99 and those peak bursts?
3) Pricing/commit impact: what is an estimated monthly cost delta for Dedicated versus Hosted at that scale?

We can do Thu 10am PT — Alex and I are available. Also, can you include the test plan (load profile + success criteria) in advance so our infra team can review?

Best,
Sofia Alvarez
Head of Platform Engineering | FinPay
sofia@finpay.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Alvarez <sofia@finpay.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency & throughput next steps

Hi Sofia — great questions. Quick answers & plan below.

Q1 — p99 behavior (Hosted vs Dedicated)
- Hosted: good for validation; typical p95 is low, but p99 tail can be higher due to multi-tenant scheduling and cold-starts under bursty loads. For models in the 70B range, we typically see p99 in Hosted vary ~150–300ms depending on sequence length and concurrency.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools + warm long-lived workers reduce tail significantly. For your 64–128 token profile, Dedicated commonly achieves p99 ~90–130ms depending on model/quantization and batching settings. That maps favorably to your 120ms target when sized correctly.

Q2 — recommended minimal reserved capacity
- For the spike profile (avg 2k tokens/sec, peaks 4–5k tokens/sec, 250 concurrent): recommend a starting footprint of 2 reserved GPU workers (NVIDIA A100 equivalent) with autoscale headroom for burst to 3–4 workers. We will size exactly after a 2-hour spike test that reproduces your peak.

Q3 — pricing/commit impact
- Hosted: pay-as-you-go; lower upfront but unit cost is higher at scale. Good for pilot.
- Dedicated: monthly commit for reserved GPUs — higher fixed cost but lower per-token unit economics and consistent latency. I can put together an estimated delta for the recommended footprint and send by EOD for your review.

Proposed test plan (summary)
- Objective: validate 120ms p99 for 64–128 token UI requests and measure tail under 300-concurrency bursts.
- Load profile: steady-state 2k tokens/sec for 30m, then 30m of repeated 5-min bursts to 4–5k tokens/sec, multiple repeats (total 2 hours).
- Success criteria: p99 <= 120ms for 90% of test windows during bursts; acceptable error rate <0.5%.

I'll attach a more detailed test plan and a preliminary cost estimate before our meeting. Meeting confirmed Thu, Nov 19 at 10am PT — Marissa will join for pricing.

Thanks —
Neha

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Heads up — FinPay (FP-2026-087) will likely move to Dedicated if we can demonstrate p99 ~120ms in the spike test. Action items: 

- Marissa: please prepare a 1-page pricing delta (Hosted vs Dedicated) for the recommended 2-reserved-GPU starter footprint + burst headroom. Include 3 options: pilot (Hosted), reserved (monthly commit), and hybrid (Hosted + Dedicated fallback).
- Dylan: can infra team provision a short Dedicated trial environment and support the 2-hour spike test? If possible, schedule a warmup window to reduce cold-start noise. Also log telemetry hooks we need (p95/p99, worker queue depth, batch sizes).
- Neha (me): I'll send the detailed test plan and the cost estimate to Sofia/Alex and lock the trial test window.

No discounts approved yet — price guidance only. If FinPay asks for a discount tied to a 12-month commit, we'll route to sales leadership.

Thanks —
Neha
